0: tune_batch_size: Increase batch size modestly, keeping learning rate and other settings fixed. Larger batches may reduce gradient noise and improve macro validation HR@10. The five-epoch baseline provides no reliable convergence evidence, so treat this as an isolated batch-size experiment.
1: tune_lr_batch_scheduler: Test a modestly larger batch with a proportionally smaller increase in learning rate, brief warmup, and gradual learning-rate decay. This coupled setup may improve early optimization and later ranking refinement. Preserve the configured epoch budget; judge improvement by benchmark macro validation HR@10.
2: tune_num_layers: Add one SASRec transformer block while holding embedding width and optimization settings fixed. Additional depth may capture higher-order item transitions and improve macro validation HR@10. Keep the increase small because the baseline provides no evidence that substantially greater capacity is needed, and update the predictor writer to reconstruct the trained depth.
3: tune_num_heads: Increase attention heads to the next compatible count that divides the existing embedding width, leaving depth and embedding size fixed. More heads may capture distinct sequential relationships and improve macro validation HR@10, though narrower heads could limit gains. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the trained head count.
